record.original_question: (V. V. Uspenskii). A Hausdorff topological group G is called minimal if it does not admit a strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology. A topological group is called Raikov complete if its two-sided uniform structure is complete. It is known that a finite direct product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups is again minimal. Is it true that an arbitrary Cartesian product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups remains minimal? It is known that an arbitrary Cartesian product of centre-free minimal topological groups is minimal(M. Megrelishvili, Topology Appl., 62, no. 1(1995), 1–19).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Hausdorff topological group $G$ is called minimal if it admits no strictly coarser Hausdorff group topology. A topological group is called Raikov complete if it is complete with respect to its two-sided uniform structure (the supremum of the left and right uniformities).

It is known that:
(i) any finite direct product of Raikov complete minimal topological groups is again minimal;
(ii) any Cartesian product of centre-free minimal topological groups is minimal.

Question: Is it true that, for every family $\{G_i : i \in I\}$ of Raikov complete minimal Hausdorff topological groups, the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} G_i$ (endowed with the product topology and the coordinate-wise group operation) is again a minimal topological group?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing question of Uspenskij on whether arbitrary products of Raikov complete minimal groups are minimal. Only partial positive results are known, e.g., products of complete totally minimal groups are minimal, and products of centre-free minimal groups are minimal. Recent work (e.g., "Products of locally minimal groups," 2022) continues to give partial answers, indicating the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Products of locally minimal groups
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Uspenskij's problem on products of complete minimal groups and provides partial positive answers.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains a subject of ongoing research with only partial answers available.

status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among unsolved problems.
